property_summary: After any Put call, the stored unlockTime for the sender is never less than the current block timestamp (reference enforces acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant can set it to a past value and thus violate this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value, after calling Put the stored unlockTime for the caller is >= the block timestamp (reference enforces max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns _unlockTime unconditionally can store a time < block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs and thus violate this invariant.

For any caller, when they call Put with any _unlockTime and any payable value, the reference contract guarantees that Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after the call (it stores max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that unconditionally assigns _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime values (past times), breaking this invariant.

For any caller and any input to Put, the reference contract ensures that if the caller sends any positive ether then Acc[caller].balance increases by that amount and Acc[caller].unlockTime is never decreased by that Put call compared to the prior stored unlockTime; the mutant can set unlockTime to an arbitrary (older) value and thus can decrease stored unlockTime for some inputs.

For any caller, any msg.value and any _unlockTime, the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime >= previous Acc[caller].unlockTime (Put never decreases the stored unlockTime); the mutant can decrease unlockTime by assigning an older _unlockTime, violating this monotonicity for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put with value>0 the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime in the reference contract is at least as large as the pre-call block.timestamp or the provided _unlockTime (i.e., it never resets to an earlier time); the mutant unconditionally sets unlockTime to block.timestamp which can make it smaller than the intended _unlockTime, breaking the rule for some inputs.

After any Put by any sender with any nonzero value and any _unlockTime, the reference contract ensures Acc[sender].unlockTime >= _unlockTime (i.e., it never sets unlockTime earlier than the provided _unlockTime), whereas the mutant always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp and can make Acc[sender].unlockTime < _unlockTime for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, after calling Put the reference contract sets Acc[depositor].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (i.e., it never sets unlockTime earlier than now), but the mutant can set unlockTime == block.timestamp which may be strictly less than a previously set larger unlockTime (violating preservation of a previously-larger unlockTime) — specifically: if a caller first sets a future unlockTime > block.timestamp and then calls Put with value>0 and a smaller _unlockTime, the reference preserves the previously larger unlockTime (it remains >= block.timestamp and >= the provided smaller _unlockTime), whereas the mutant resets it to block.timestamp, making it smaller than the prior future unlockTime.

For any depositor, if they first set a future unlockTime by calling Put and then later call Put again with any value, the reference contract preserves the previously set unlockTime (it remains strictly greater than block.timestamp when previously set in future), whereas the mutant resets unlockTime to block.timestamp, making it smaller than that previously set future time.

For any depositor who first sets a future unlockTime via Put, a subsequent Put that supplies any smaller _unlockTime must not decrease the stored unlockTime below the previously set future value; the mutant resets unlockTime to block.timestamp and thus can make it smaller than the prior future value.

After any Put(sender, value, unlock) call, the stored unlockTime for sender is at least block.timestamp (i.e., never earlier than the current block time); the mutant inverts the comparison and can set unlockTime < block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, breaking this rule.

After any successful Put call, the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp (i.e., unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant inverts the comparison and can set unlockTime < block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, violating this rule.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put with any payment the contract's stored unlockTime for that caller equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) (i.e., it is never less than both _unlockTime and block.timestamp); the mutant which uses min(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) can set unlockTime < _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp or set unlockTime < block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, violating this rule.

For any caller, calling Put with any _unlockTime and any payable value sets Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime to either _unlockTime (if _unlockTime >= block.timestamp) or block.timestamp (if _unlockTime < block.timestamp) — i.e., the stored unlockTime is equal to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant using min can set unlockTime < block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, violating this rule.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and any payable value, after Put completes the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns the lesser of _unlockTime and block.timestamp can set unlockTime < block.timestamp when _unlockTime is in the past, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any msg.value, a single call to Put increases the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly the msg.value supplied (i.e., newBalance - oldBalance == msg.value); the mutant doubles the increment and thus violates this for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposited msg.value, a single call to Put increases Acc[caller].balance by exactly the deposited msg.value; the mutant that adds msg.value twice makes the observed increase greater than msg.value for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit amount > 0, the contract's stored Acc[depositor].balance increases by exactly the sent msg.value (new - old == msg.value); the mutant that adds msg.value twice causes the stored balance to increase by 2*msg.value for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any sent ether amount, calling Put increases Acc[caller].balance by at most msg.value (i.e., newBalance - oldBalance <= msg.value); the mutant that adds msg.value twice can make the increase exceed msg.value for some inputs, violating this bound.

For any depositor address and any nonzero ether value, calling Put increases that depositor's recorded Acc balance by exactly the amount of ether sent; the mutant that adds msg.value twice makes the recorded increase sometimes equal to 2*msg.value, violating this equality for some inputs.

Rule: After any successful Put(uint _unlockTime) by an account with value >=0, the contract's Acc(account).unlockTime in the correct contract is set to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp), whereas the mutant omits updating unlockTime so the stored unlockTime does not increase to that max — the reference always sets unlockTime to at least block.timestamp while the mutant can leave it lower for some inputs.

For any account performing Put with a positive value, the correct contract always ensures Acc(account).unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it sets unlockTime to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)), whereas the mutant may leave unlockTime unchanged and thus < block.timestamp for some inputs after Put, allowing premature Collect; the test fuzzes actor, value, and _unlockTime and asserts unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put.

After a Put(...) call that sends any positive ether, the reference contract always sets Acc(actor).unlockTime to at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., >= block.timestamp), whereas the mutant that omits updating unlockTime can leave it lower and thus violate that invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any Put(...) invocation (with any value), after Put completes the reference contract guarantees Acc(caller).unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it sets unlockTime = max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that deletes that update can leave unlockTime unchanged and thus < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any Put(uint _unlockTime) call funded with msg.value > 0, the reference contract ensures Acc(caller).unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put (it sets unlockTime = max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that omits updating unlockTime can leave it unchanged and thus < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

After depositing >= MinSum and setting unlockTime in the future, the caller can withdraw that amount (Collect succeeds) iff their stored balance (Acc[msg.sender].balance) is >= requested amount and unlockTime passed — i.e., eligibility depends on the account's stored balance, not the caller's wallet balance.

Collect reverts exactly when either the caller's stored account balance is less than the requested amount, or the account's unlockTime has not passed, or the stored balance is below MinSum — eligibility depends on the contract's stored Acc[msg.sender].balance, not the caller's external wallet balance.

If the caller's external (EOA) wallet balance is less than MinSum then Collect must not revert solely because of that; i.e., Collect's success depends on the contract's stored account balance and not on msg.sender.balance.

Collect should never revert when the caller's stored account balance Acc[msg.sender].balance is >= MinSum, >= requested amount, and unlockTime has passed (regardless of the caller EOA's external wallet balance).
